title: 第四章 消失的村庄第六章 铁炉堡
slug: 黯潮纪元异世界的崛起
lines: 消息在第三日清晨传到了银月城。传令兵是从铁荒原北部一路换马奔驰而来，抵达北门时胯下那匹栗色战马口吐白沫瘫倒在石板上，挣扎了两下就没再站起来。传令兵本人双腿内侧被马鞍磨得血肉模糊，血从皮靴上沿渗出，但他没有先去医疗所——他直接冲进了王宫。十五分钟后，紧急军事会议在王宫议事厅召开。
陈默没有列席资格，他从训练场上骑士们的低声议论中拼凑大致轮廓。铁荒原北部三个边境村庄在三天前同一时段失联——不是被攻陷，不是被屠戮，是同时从联络地图上消失。铁王国派出的第一支侦察队进入其中一座村庄后也没有出来。银月城灯塔守夜人记录到西北方向紫色光芒一闪，持续时间约三秒，正对应三个村庄所在位置。
“三个村庄，差不多两千口人。“德文教官把消息在训练场上传达时声音压得很低很沉，“不是死了，是消失了。侦察兵抵达时发现房子里一切完好——桌上还摆着吃到一半的饭，炉灶里还有余温，晾衣绳上的衣服还在滴水。但没有一个人。两千口人像被同时从画面上抠掉了。科尔曼副团长带队，圣殿骑士团出二十人，铁王国那边会派向导接应。“他的目光扫过在场所有人，落在陈默身上，“雷诺·艾德伍德，你算一个。“
陈默没想到自己这个还没痊愈的新兵会被点名。“为什么是我？“
“大法师说该让你看看黯潮到底是什么。“德文这句话没有任何情绪，但陈默听出了背后的潜台词：这不是建议，是通知，而且是阿尔德里奇的意见。那个老法师已经把他盯上了——不是监视，是观察。像一个站在高处的人看着山谷中一颗被掷入水面的石子。
“明天拂晓出发。“德文说完这句话就转身走了，背影在训练场沙地上拖出一道被朝阳拉长的斜影。
黄昏时分陈默在装备库做准备工作。其实没什么好准备——他连自己的盔甲都没有。德文从仓库角落翻出一套相对合身的链甲衫和一顶铁盔，配一把制式长剑和一面圆盾，外加三天口粮、一个水囊和一卷绷带。他把链甲衫套上试了试，肩膀位置略窄，雷诺的骨架比他想象中的肩宽要小。
艾莉西亚在装备库门口等着，她也被编入了侦察队。她背靠门框站着，夕阳从她身后照过来，在石板地上拉出一个瘦长的人影。“怕吗？“她的问题出乎意料地直接。
陈默想了想怎么回答。按照正常人的逻辑他应该怕——他才来这个世界第四天，连通用语都还没完全熟练，就要上前线进行调查任务。但他发现自己此刻的心态不是恐惧。“说实在话，更多是好奇。就像看到了一个学术空白——那道紫色光芒到底是什么？两千人怎么同时消失的？如果黯潮不是军队也不是瘟疫，那它是什么？我在脑子里跑了三遍可能的方向，没有一个以前的知识能直接套用。这种'找不到套用框架'的感觉——反而让我冷静。“
艾莉西亚看着他，那眼神里有一种复杂的东西。“你知道我第一次上前线是什么感觉吗？“她没等他回答就说了下去，“害怕到想吐。不是怕死——是怕没准备好就死了。但我那时还对圣光有坚定信仰，我觉得——诸神与我同在，圣光会接住我。“她低下头，看着自己胸前那枚鹰翼环绕满月的徽章，手指在铁质徽面纹路上无意识地划过。
“现在呢？“
这次沉默持续了很长时间——长到夕阳从她肩头滑到了腰间。“现在我什么都不确定。我不知道那道光来自哪里，不知道是谁在回应我的祈祷，不知道我哥哥为它而死——是不是死在一个谎言上。“她把徽章从胸口解下来握在手心，掌心合拢。“但我确定了一件事——如果我必须选择相信什么东西，我选择相信我自己亲眼看到的东西。“
陈默看着她。这个年轻女骑士的信仰正在从根部开始松动，但她没有崩溃——她在松动中找到了一种新的锚。不是教条，不是经文，是对自身感知的诚实。这比任何一种信仰都更坚固。他想说点什么，但最终什么都没说。有时候人不说话，本身就是一种理解。
“明早路上如果遇到——任何不寻常的东西，不要逞强。“艾莉西亚换了一种语气，把话题拉回任务层面，“我比你有经验，我可以走在前面。“
陈默几乎脱口而出“我也可以走在你前面“，但他说出口的是另一句话：“一个人挡在前面只是换了个站位，两个人并肩才是换了个思路。“
次日拂晓，二十人侦察队在北门集结。带队的是圣殿骑士团副团长科尔曼——一个四十岁左右、灰白头发的瘦削骑士，沉默寡言，目光像鹰一样锐利且从不长时间停留在任何人脸上。除了陈默和艾莉西亚，其余都是经验丰富的老兵——铁盔上的凹痕、剑柄上磨损的缠带、手臂上缝合过的旧伤疤，每一处都在无声说话。

出发前科尔曼把所有人召集到城门口，背对刚亮起来的天光简短吩咐：“我们的任务是勘察三个村庄的失踪现场。不交战，不追查，只看、记录、带回情报。这是命令。“他顿了顿，扫过每一张脸，像在检查每个人的眼神中有没有“我已经慌了“的信号。“银月城流传着很多关于黯潮的说法，绝大部分是假的。我在前线待过八年，我可以告诉你们黯潮不是军队、不是野兽、不是任何能用刀杀死的东西。它是一层覆盖在世界表面的'异物'——你走进黯潮覆盖区，就走进了一个不属于我们这个世界的空间。那里没有声音，没有气味，没有风。只有压力——无形的、从四面八方挤压你的压力。在黯潮区域待久了人会做出奇怪的事：大笑不止、痛哭不止、挖自己的眼珠。教廷说是恶魔诱惑。我不反驳。“他没说他不反驳是因为他不信，还是因为他不能公开反驳。
二十人翻身上马，沿北方官道缓缓出了银月城。陈默骑在队伍中段，雷诺的马术肌肉记忆让他的骑姿看起来比实际精神状态稳定得多——他的脑子里在疯狂吸收沿途信息：地名、路标、植被变化、路人反应。漫长的土路在晨光下蜿蜒伸展，前方是未知的边境和已经消失的两千条人命。

第一日行军波澜不惊。沿古老商道向西北行进约一百二十里，途经几个仍然安全的小村落。村民看到骑士团经过纷纷从田里直起腰挥手欢呼——对他们来说圣殿骑士团代表安全与希望，白金色的徽章等同于“诸神没有忘记我“的视觉保证。陈默看着那些挥手的面孔，一种说不清的感觉堵在胸口。这些人不知道圣光背后有不可知的代价，不知道头顶星空正在悄悄位移，不知道北边三个村庄已经连同两千口人一起蒸发。他们活在一种精心维护的无知中——而无知本身，正在从北方一寸一寸被蚕食。
傍晚队伍在灰桥镇歇脚，一个小镇，约三百来户，依一座石拱老桥两岸散落而建。镇长是个六十多岁驼背笑容明亮的老人，热情接待了骑士团。晚饭时陈默借机和他聊了几句，话题从一个简单问题切入：“镇长先生，您在这里住了多少年？“
“一辈子，六十二年，我们家从爷爷辈起就住灰桥镇。“老人笑呵呵地说，缺了一颗门牙但眼神很锐。
“您这几年注意到边境有什么异常吗？“

笑容淡了一些。老人沉默了很久——那种沉默不是犹豫，是在回忆中向下挖掘。“说不上来具体是什么。但过去一年，怪事越来越多。先是井水变苦，然后是地里的麦子收成越来越差——同样的种子同样的土地，就是长不起来。“他压低声音，像是怕被什么东西听到，“然后最奇怪的是——晚上经常能听到一种声音。像有人在地底下说话，又像风穿过很窄的石缝发出呼号。但你仔细一听——那不是说话也不是风声。它是一种——“他指了指自己左胸位置，“你听到它时这个地方会发闷。像有只手在捏心脏。“
陈默的神经紧绷了一下。“这种情况持续多久了？“
“大约半年。从最开始只有靠北边那几户能听到，到现在整个镇子都能听到。而且声音越来越——怎么说——越来越近了。“
“教廷来过吗？“

老人的表情变得古怪。“三个月前，一队穿白袍的教士来过。他们在镇外空地做了一场圣光净化仪式，说可以净化土地。仪式结束后就走了。那一周声音确实变小了——但那一周镇上疯了三个人。都是认识了几十年的好人：一个晚上突然冲出屋子在街上大喊'它们来了它们来了'，另外两个在自家厨房里拿菜刀砍自己，都没救过来。“他端着碗的枯瘦手指在轻微颤抖，“其中一个是老朋友的妻子，她每天去教堂做三次礼拜。全教堂最虔诚的就是她。“
陈默沉默了很久。他开始理解一个他不愿接受但不得不接受的可能性：在这个世界，“虔诚“可能不是免疫力，而是信号放大器。越虔诚的人越容易成为某种力量的接收器——因为虔诚的本质是“放下自我敞开心灵“，而这种“敞开“恰好为某种不可名状的信号提供了最优接收条件。
“谢谢您，镇长先生。这几天如果又听到那种声音——尽量不去回想它。如果有人突然说'它们来了'之类的话，立刻带那个人离开镇子去开阔地方待着。“他没有解释原因，因为他不确定自己的直觉对不对，但他有一种从数据中涌现出来的预感：那些声音不全是幻听。它们是信标。每次有人听到，某个看不见的“坐标“就被更新了一次。而当那个坐标精确到一定程度时——收信人就会来敲门。
第二日黎明，队伍离开灰桥镇继续北上。道路从商道变成狭窄的土路，两侧的橡树和榆树逐渐被低矮扭曲的灌木取代。上午过半时他们经过一座废弃农场——栅栏被什么东西从地下往上撕裂，木桩断口不是劈裂而是像被从内部撑爆，截面呈现蜂窝状的孔洞结构。科尔曼下马检查了不到一分钟就命令继续前进——他的表情告诉所有人他见过这个。

傍晚扎营前队伍在一条干涸河床边停了一刻钟。河床上没有水，但淤泥中有成群结队的鸟兽足迹全部指向南方——不是迁徙方向，是逃离方向。陈默蹲下用手指探了一下淤泥温度，凉的。不是被太阳晒凉——是那种被什么东西吸走了地热的凉。他站起身时忽然听到一声极其微弱的金属嗡鸣从北面飘来——像有人在地平线另一端敲了一口比银月城大教堂更大的钟，但只能听到尾音中最细最远的那一根泛音。他看了科尔曼一眼，老兵已经听到了。他没有说话——但他把长剑从腰间解下握在了手里，这是他从离开银月城以来第一次这么做。
次日午后，队伍抵达雪松镇——最后一个仍有人驻守的边境村落，再往北一日就是第一个失联点白石村。雪松镇比灰桥镇更残破，村口木栅栏上有新鲜火烧痕迹，几座房屋的茅草屋顶塌了半边，街上零星几个留守老人在自家门口发愣。其他居民都撤走了——铁王国在村庄失联后疏散了后方所有人口。科尔曼决定在雪松镇驻扎一晚，明早推进至白石村。

安排完哨位后陈默独自在镇子外围走了一圈。他注意到一些不讲逻辑的细节：水井水面漂着一层灰色油膜，在光下泛出虹彩但毫无晃动——不是浮油，是水面上长了一层肉眼可见的膜；外围树木叶片呈现出一种不自然的暗紫色，不是季节变化，是组织被某种外来细胞侵入后的病态反应。他蹲下身抓了一把土，泥土碎成粉末，干燥到反常。土中夹杂着极细小的透明晶体——像被高温熔过的玻璃渣，但有肉眼隐约可见的精密纹路。不是天然晶体棱角——是一种有规律的、像是被纳米级刀刃刻上去的线条。
他取一小块布包了些泥土和晶体收藏入怀，站起身时心跳比正常快了好几档。那些晶体表面纹路有可能是某种微型符文——如果真是这样，它代表一种能力和意图：有某种实体能在微观层面改写物质的基础结构，并在宏观世界投射其意志。这不是自然灾害，不是动物侵袭，不是常规意义上的“敌人“。它是一种——他暂时找不到比“污染“更准确但又不完全准确的词。那种被“看到“的感觉又回来了。
回到招待所后他从行囊中翻出一本空白羊皮手册——这是出发前从奥利弗书店买的。他翻开第一页，用中文写下：
“穿越第五日。三个村庄消失。白石村明日勘察。土壤中发现微型未知晶体。直觉——这不是攻击。这是某种更大进程的前沿信号。待验证。“
他把手册揣进怀里。在这个世界，“记忆“本身就是一种风险——被记录下来的异常观察如果被教廷看到，足够被定义为异端。但他必须记录。他是这个世界上唯一能站在两套知识体系交叉点上审视一切的人，如果他也不记录，那些关键信息就会无声沉没——而那个过程中如果漏掉任何一个关键信息，代价可能不是他的命，是所有人的。
content_en:
The news reached Silvermoon City in the early morning of the third day. The messenger came all the way from the north of the Iron Wasteland, changing horses and galloping. When they arrived at the north gate, the chestnut-colored horse was frothing at the mouth and collapsed on the stone slab. After struggling twice, it didn't stand up again. The messenger's inner legs were bruised and bruised by the saddle, and blood seeped from the upper edges of his leather boots. However, he did not go to the medical center first - he rushed directly into the palace. Fifteen minutes later, an emergency military meeting was held in the palace chamber.
Chen Mo was not qualified to attend, so he pieced together the general outline from the whispers of the knights on the training ground. Three border villages in the northern part of the Iron Waste lost contact at the same time three days ago - they were either captured or massacred, but they disappeared from the contact map at the same time. The first reconnaissance team sent by the Iron Kingdom did not come out even after entering one of the villages. The night watchman of the Silvermoon City Lighthouse recorded a flash of purple light in the northwest, lasting about three seconds, which corresponded to the location of the three villages.
"Three villages, almost two thousand people." Instructor Devin's voice was very low when conveying the news on the training ground. "He is not dead, but disappeared. When the scout arrived, he found that everything in the house was intact - there was still a half-eaten meal on the table, there was still warmth in the stove, and clothes on the clothesline It was still dripping. But there was no one. Two thousand portraits were cut out from the screen at the same time. Deputy Captain Coleman led the team, and the Iron Kingdom sent a guide to help. "His eyes fell on Chen Mo, "Reno Edwood."
Chen Mo didn't expect that he, a recruit who had not recovered yet, would be named. "Why me?"
"The Archmage said that you should see what the Dark Tide is." There was no emotion in Devin's words, but Chen Mo heard the subtext behind it: this was not a suggestion, but a notice, and it was Aldridge's opinion. The old mage had already set his sights on him - not for surveillance, but for observation. Like a person standing on a high place looking at a stone thrown into the water in the valley.
"Leave at dawn tomorrow." After Devin said these words, he turned around and left, his back dragging a slanting shadow stretched by the rising sun on the sand of the training ground.
***
At dusk, Chen Mo was making preparations in the equipment warehouse. There was really nothing to prepare for - he didn't even have his own armor. Devin dug out a relatively well-fitting chainmail shirt and an iron helmet from the corner of the warehouse, along with a standard long sword and a round shield, plus three days of rations, a water bag and a roll of bandages. He put the chain mail shirt on and tried it on. The shoulders were slightly narrower, and Renault's frame was smaller than he expected.
Alicia was waiting at the entrance of the equipment warehouse. She was also included in the reconnaissance team. She stood with her back against the doorframe, and the setting sun shone from behind her, drawing out a slender figure on the stone floor. "Are you afraid?" Her question was unexpectedly direct.
Chen Mo thought about how to answer. According to the logic of normal people, he should be afraid - he was only on his fourth day in this world, and he was not even fully proficient in the common language, so he was about to go to the front line to conduct an investigation mission. But he found that his state of mind at the moment was not fear. "To be honest, it's more out of curiosity. It's like seeing an academic blank - what is that purple light? How did two thousand people disappear at the same time? If the Dark Tide is not an army or a plague, what is it? I ran three possible directions in my mind, but none of the previous knowledge can be directly applied. This feeling of 'cannot find an application framework' - actually makes me calm down."
Alicia looked at him, with something complicated in her eyes. "Do you know what it was like when I went to the front line for the first time?" She continued without waiting for his answer. "I was so scared that I wanted to vomit. It wasn't that I was afraid of death - I was afraid of dying before I was ready. But I still had firm faith in the Holy Light at that time. I felt that the gods were with me and the Holy Light would catch me." She lowered her head and looked at the emblem with eagle wings surrounding the full moon on her chest, and her fingers unconsciously traced the lines on the iron emblem.
"What now?"
The silence lasted for a long time - so long that the sunset slipped from her shoulders to her waist. "I'm not sure of anything now. I don't know where that light came from, who answered my prayers, or whether my brother died for it—if he died for a lie." She took the badge off her chest and held it in her hands, clasping her palms together. “But I’m sure of one thing – if I have to choose to believe something, I choose to believe what I see with my own eyes.”
Chen Mo looked at her. The young female knight's faith was beginning to loosen from its roots, but she did not collapse—she found a new anchor in the loosening. Not dogma, not scripture, but honesty about one’s own perception. This is stronger than any other belief. He wanted to say something, but ended up saying nothing. Sometimes people don't speak, which is a kind of understanding in itself.
"If you encounter anything unusual on the road tomorrow morning, don't show off." Alicia changed her tone and brought the topic back to the task level, "I have more experience than you, I can go ahead."
Chen Mo almost blurted out, "I can walk in front of you," but what he said was another sentence: "One person standing in front is just a change of position, two people standing side by side is a change of thinking."
***
At dawn the next day, a twenty-man reconnaissance team assembled at the north gate. The team was led by Coleman, the deputy head of the Knights Templar - a thin knight with gray hair in his forties, taciturn, with eyes as sharp as an eagle that never stayed on anyone's face for a long time. Except for Chen Mo and Alicia, the others were all experienced veterans - the dents on the iron helmets, the frayed straps on the sword hilts, and the old stitched scars on the arms, every part spoke silently.
Before setting off, Coleman summoned everyone to the city gate and gave a brief instruction with his back to the newly dawned sky: "Our mission is to investigate the missing scenes in three villages. No fighting, no tracing, just watching, recording, and bringing back information. This is an order." He paused and scanned every face, as if checking everyone's eyes for the "I'm already panicked" signal. "There are many rumors about the Dark Tide circulating in Silvermoon City, most of which are false. I have been on the front line for eight years, and I can tell you that the Dark Tide is not an army, a beast, or anything that can be killed with a knife. It is a layer of 'foreign matter' covering the surface of the world - when you walk into the Dark Tide coverage area, you enter a space that does not belong to our world. There is no sound, no smell, no wind. There is only invisible pressure that squeezes you from all sides. People will do strange things if they stay in the dark tide area for a long time: laughing, crying, and gouging their own eyes. "I didn't say that he didn't refute it because he didn't believe it, or because he couldn't refute it publicly.
Twenty people got on their horses and slowly left Silver Moon City along the northern official road. Chen Mo was riding in the middle of the group. Renault's equestrian muscle memory made his riding posture look much more stable than his actual mental state - his mind was frantically absorbing information along the way: place names, road signs, changes in vegetation, reactions of passers-by. The long dirt road winds and stretches under the morning light. In front of it is an unknown border and two thousand lives that have disappeared.
***
The march on the first day was uneventful. Travel northwest along the ancient trade road for about 120 miles, passing through several small villages that are still safe. Villagers stood up from the fields and waved and cheered when they saw the Knights passing by - for them, the Knights Templar represent safety and hope, and the white-gold badge is equivalent to the visual guarantee that "the gods have not forgotten me." Chen Mo looked at the waving faces, and an indescribable feeling filled his chest. These people don't know that there is an unknown price behind the holy light, they don't know that the stars above their heads are quietly shifting, and they don't know that three villages to the north have evaporated along with 2,000 people. They live in a carefully maintained ignorance - and ignorance itself is being eaten away inch by inch from the north.
In the evening, the team rested in Huiqiao Town, a small town with about 300 households scattered along both sides of an old stone arch bridge. The mayor, a hunchbacked old man in his sixties with a bright smile, warmly received the knights. During dinner, Chen Mo took the opportunity to chat with him for a few words. The topic started with a simple question: "Mr. Mayor, how many years have you lived here?"
"My whole life, sixty-two years, our family has lived in Huiqiao Town since my grandfather's generation." The old man said with a smile, one front tooth missing but his eyes were sharp.
"Have you noticed anything unusual at the border in the past few years?"
The smile faded a bit. The old man was silent for a long time - that silence was not hesitation, but digging deeper in memories. "I can't say what it is specifically. But in the past year, there have been more and more strange things. First, the well water has become bitter, and then the wheat harvest in the field has become worse and worse - the same seeds, the same land, just can't grow." He lowered his voice, as if he was afraid of being heard by something, "Then the strangest thing is - at night You can often hear a sound like someone talking underground, or like the wind whistling through a very narrow crack in the rocks. But if you listen carefully, it's not a voice, it's a kind of sound. "When you hear it, it feels like a hand is squeezing your heart."
Chen Mo's nerves tensed up. "How long has this been going on?"
"About half a year. At first, only a few households on the north side could hear it, but now the whole town can hear it. And the sound is getting - how should I say - getting closer."
"Has the Holy See been here?"
The old man's expression became strange. "Three months ago, a group of priests in white robes came. They performed a Holy Light Purification Ceremony in the open space outside the town, saying it could purify the land. After the ceremony, they left. The voice did become quieter that week - but three people went crazy in the town that week. They were all good people who had known each other for decades: one night suddenly rushed He went out to the street and shouted, 'They are coming, they are coming', and the other two were cutting themselves with kitchen knives, but they were not able to save themselves." His skinny fingers holding the bowl were trembling slightly. "One of them is the wife of an old friend. She is the most devout person in the church. "
Chen Mo was silent for a long time. He began to understand a possibility that he was unwilling to accept but had to accept: In this world, "piety" may not be immunity, but a signal amplifier. The more pious a person is, the easier it is to become a receiver of some kind of power - because the essence of piety is to "let go of oneself and open the heart", and this "openness" happens to provide optimal reception conditions for some indescribable signals.
"Thank you, Mr. Mayor. If you hear that sound again these days - try not to think about it. If someone suddenly says, 'They are coming' or something like that, take that person out of the town immediately to an open area." He did not explain the reason, because he was not sure whether his intuition was right, but he had a hunch emerging from the data: those sounds were not all auditory hallucinations. They are beacons. Every time someone hears it, some invisible "coordinate" is updated. And when the coordinates are accurate to a certain extent - the recipient will knock on the door.
***
At dawn the next day, the team left Huiqiao Town and continued northward. The road changed from a commercial road to a narrow dirt road, and the oak and elm trees on both sides were gradually replaced by low and twisted shrubs. In the middle of the morning, they passed an abandoned farm - the fence was torn upwards by something from the ground. The broken wooden piles were not split but seemed to have been exploded from the inside. The cross-section showed a honeycomb-like structure of holes. Coleman dismounted and inspected for less than a minute before giving the order to move on—his expression told everyone he had seen this before.
Before setting up camp in the evening, the team stopped for a quarter of an hour beside a dry river bed. There was no water on the river bed, but there were swarms of bird and animal tracks in the mud, all pointing south—not in the direction of migration, but in the direction of escape. Chen Mo squatted down and used his fingers to check the temperature of the mud. It was cold. It's not like being cooled by the sun - it's the kind of coolness that's been sucked away from the earth's heat by something. When he stood up, he suddenly heard an extremely weak metallic buzz coming from the north - it was like someone was ringing a bell bigger than the Silvermoon City Cathedral on the other side of the horizon, but only the thinnest and farthest overtone of the tail tone could be heard. He glanced at Coleman, and the veteran had heard. He didn't speak - but he took off the sword from his waist and held it in his hand. This was the first time he had done so since leaving Silvermoon City.
***
In the afternoon of the next day, the team arrived at Cedar Town, the last border village where people were still stationed. One day further north was Baishi Village, the first point of loss of contact. Cedar Town is even more dilapidated than Huiqiao Town. There are fresh fire marks on the wooden fence at the entrance of the village, half of the thatched roofs of several houses have collapsed, and a few left-behind elderly people are in a daze at the door of their homes on the street. The other residents were evacuated - the Iron Kingdom evacuated all the population in the rear after losing contact with the village. Coleman decided to camp at Cedartown for one night and advance to Whitestone Village in the morning.
After arranging the sentry posts, Chen Mo walked around the outside of the town alone. He noticed some illogical details: there was a gray oil film floating on the water surface of the well, which glowed iridescent under the light but did not sway at all - it was not an oil slick, but a film visible to the naked eye on the water surface; the leaves of the surrounding trees showed an unnatural dark purple, which was not a seasonal change, but a pathological reaction after the tissue was invaded by some foreign cells. He knelt down and grabbed a handful of soil. The soil crumbled into powder and was abnormally dry. The soil is mixed with extremely fine transparent crystals - like glass slag that has been melted by high temperature, but with precise lines that are vaguely visible to the naked eye. It's not a natural crystal edge - it's a regular line that looks like it's been carved by a nanoscale blade.
He took a small piece of cloth and wrapped some soil and crystals in his arms. When he stood up, his heart beat several times faster than normal. The lines on the surface of those crystals may be some kind of micro-runes - if so, it represents an ability and intention: there is some entity that can rewrite the basic structure of matter at the micro level and project its will on the macro world. This is not a natural disaster, not an animal attack, or an "enemy" in the conventional sense. It's a kind of - he can't find a word that is more accurate than "pollution" but not completely accurate. That feeling of being "seen" is back.
After returning to the guest house, he dug out a blank parchment booklet from his luggage - which he had bought from Oliver's Bookstore before departure. He turned to the first page and wrote in Chinese:
"Traveling through the fifth day. Three villages disappeared. Baishi Village will be surveyed tomorrow. Micro unknown crystals were found in the soil. Intuition - this is not an attack. This is a frontier signal of some larger process. To be verified."
He put the manual in his arms. In this world, "memory" itself is a risk - anomalous observations recorded are enough to be defined as heresy if seen by the Holy See. But he must record it. He is the only person in the world who can stand at the intersection of two sets of knowledge systems and examine everything. If he does not record it, the key information will sink silently - and if any key information is missed in the process, the price may not be his life, but everyone's.
